page: Vultr vc2-8c-32gb is a General Purpose virtual machine from the Cloud Compute family. It features an Intel x86_64 processor running at 2.0 GHz, configured with 8 shared vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled and consists of a 640 GB NVMe SSD. No dedicated GPU hardware is included.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance profile shaped by the shared CPU allocation. Single-core performance is limited, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 10%. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as seen in stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU tests. Memory read bandwidth is average at 516.53 GB/sec for small cached blocks, but write bandwidth for large blocks is poor. Computational tasks such as software compilation with Clang and image processing achieve average marks, while database operations and cryptographic tasks show weaker relative performance.

Given the shared CPU architecture, this instance offers a cost-effective option for workloads requiring substantial memory and NVMe storage capacity without needing sustained, dedicated single-core CPU performance. It is suited for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, multi-threaded decompression tasks, and development environments where resource density is prioritized over raw compute speed.
